155	## First-run preflight (Decided by implementation, 2026-10-03)
156	
157	`apps/api/src/preflight.ts` runs a fixed list of checks and reports each as `ok`, `warn` (works, but something is missing or is set up on first start), or `fail` (runs will not work until it is fixed). Nothing in it changes state or starts a harness session: an existing store is inspected through the same read-only connection as startup's guard, so a refused or healthy store keeps its database and write-ahead log bytes (the `-shm` index is shared memory any reader updates).
158	
159	For an existing current, migrated store, offline model admission uses startup's catalog projection:
160	stored rows come first, with shipped seeds appended in memory only when their `(harness, model)`
161	pair is absent. A newly shipped seed can therefore satisfy `GG_DEFAULTS` before the first upgrade
162	start without being inserted by preflight. Stored metadata and disabled rows still take precedence;
163	preflight does not refresh them. Codex's disabled default remains a warning; disabled models stay
164	unavailable to execution. Missing stores use the shipped catalog; unsupported or unreadable stores
165	still fail their database check.
166	
167	| Check          | ok                                                                                                                                                            | warn                                                                                                                                                 | fail                                                                                    |
168	| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
169	| Node.js        | major version 22 only                                                                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                      | any major other than 22                                                                 |
170	| Data directory | exists and a new probe file can be created (exclusively, random name) and removed                                                                             | does not exist yet (created on first start)                                                                                                          | not a directory, unreadable, or not writable                                            |
171	| Master key     | `GG_MASTER_KEY` or `<dataDir>/master.key` decodes to 32 bytes                                                                                                 | no key yet (generated on first start; back it up)                                                                                                    | present but not a base64 32-byte key, or unreadable                                     |
172	| Database       | reachable, no pending migrations                                                                                                                              | file does not exist yet but its nearest existing ancestor is a writable directory (start creates the rest), or migrations pending (applied at start) | cannot be opened, read, or queried, or its file cannot be created                       |
173	| Harness `<id>` | `HarnessPort.preflight()` ok (Codex checks its executable and login; Claude checks native Windows CLI 2.1.285 or newer, supported flags, and Claude.ai login) | Claude is unavailable or not logged in while no Claude default is configured                                                                         | required harness not installed, not logged in, unsupported, or no harness is registered |
174	| Jev            | `jev-api-key` secret set                                                                                                                                      | no key (Jev is optional; a decision selecting it cannot run), or not checkable before the database is migrated                                       |                                                                                         |
175	| Default model  | Codex model is in its enabled catalog; a Claude default is the exact supported model and effort                                                               | configured model is in the catalog but disabled                                                                                                      | model is missing, unknown, wrong-family, or has unsupported effort                      |
176	
177	- **HTTP**: `GET /system/preflight` returns `{ ok, checks: [{ id, label, status, message }] }` for the running installation; `ok` is false when any check failed. It is not a public route: it needs a key whenever keys are required, like every other [non-public route](07-api-and-streaming.md#public-routes-decided-by-implementation-2026-10-03). `GET /harness/preflight` remains for the harness check alone.
178	- **CLI**: `node apps/api/dist/main.js --preflight` (or `pnpm --filter @graphgoblin/api preflight` after `pnpm build`) reads the same environment as the server, prints the checks as a table, and exits 0 when no check failed and 1 otherwise, without starting the server. It opens the database only when its file exists, and never creates the data directory, the key, or the database, so it is safe before the first start. `GG_DB_URL` is parsed the way libsql parses it (percent-decoded, relative, `file:///C:/...`), and the server's start creates the database file's directory as well as the data directory. The writability probe opens a new randomly named file with `wx`, so it never truncates an existing file, never follows a symlink, and removes only the file it created.
179	
180	## First API key (Decided, WP-F2, ADR-0015)
181	
182	With `GG_REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, `POST /api-keys` needs a key, so the first one cannot come from the API. Stop any API using the data directory first. `graphgoblin-api --create-api-key <name> [--scopes a,b]` (`node apps/api/dist/main.js ...`) reads the same environment as the server, takes its data-directory lock, creates the database if needed and applies migrations (as a start would), inserts a key for the local owner, prints the token once to standard output, releases the lock, and exits without starting the HTTP server. A held lock exits 1 before any database work. Nothing is logged; only the SHA-256 hash is stored. Scopes default to `*` only when `--scopes` is absent: an unknown or repeated option, a stray argument, a missing value, or a malformed scope exits 2 with the usage before anything is written. The install scripts print the command; in the container use `docker compose run --rm` with the API stopped, as shown in the guide.
183	
184	## Trigger credential boundaries (#29)
185	
186	Body-signature verification uses the exact raw bytes before decoding or parsing. The configured signing header is excluded case-insensitively from the shared `$headers` binding before dedupe and filter expressions run. Receipts and run invocations store content/signature hashes or authored business keys, never that request credential. Unsigned event and delivery headers cannot authorize a GitHub action: presets check the signed repository/object/action fields. HTTP probes remove authorization, cookie, set-cookie and API-key response headers before returning a result that may be persisted. Transport and process errors use safe diagnostic codes. This does not redact arbitrary application payload fields or make untrusted script execution safe.

1	# D172 — Preserve #448's existing disabled-model policy
2	
3	During #448 implementation at main `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`, an initial test expected disabled Codex/Claude defaults to block ordinary startup. It failed (two failures, nine passes), and source inspection disproved that assumption. Root independently read `packages/domain/src/model-resolution.ts` and `apps/api/src/container.ts`: `validateHarnessDefaults` deliberately returns only structural/effort `invalid` issues, whereas `MODEL_DISABLED` is an `unavailable` result. Startup configuration admission therefore does not reject a structurally valid default solely because its stored catalogue row is disabled. Actual model execution remains gated separately.
4	
5	Select the original narrow #448 outcome: share the pure stored-first catalogue projection without changing policy. Disabled stored metadata must win over an enabled seed. It opens the database only when its file exists, and never creates the data directory, the key, or the database, so it is safe before the first start. `GG_DB_URL` is parsed the way libsql parses it (percent-decoded, relative, `file:///C:/...`), and the server's start creates the database file's directory as well as the data directory. The writability probe opens a new randomly named file with `wx`, so it never truncates an existing file, never follows a symlink, and removes only the file it created.

# #448 independent QA: final report (continuation 02, Claude Opus 5.5)

## Verdict

**CONDITIONAL PASS.**

- **Runtime:** candidate `b45807f` does what #448 asks. Nothing in the native evidence calls for a runtime change.
- **One current blocker, documentation only:** the CHANGELOG sentence #448 adds, and the existing docs/11:157 sentence, both say "database and WAL bytes" stay unchanged. The evidence shows that a read-only open can create an **empty `-wal` and a 32 KiB `-shm`** when a WAL-mode store has no `-wal` file. Replacement wording is in §7.
- **Two failed tiers stay failed:**
  - C12: infrastructure focused suite, 55 passed / 1 failed.
  - C13: native close/EBUSY probe.
  - Both match an existing failure class. Neither is a #448 product regression.
- **Gaps:**
  - C09 and C10: parity with the base binary rests on source comparison only; the base binary was never run.
  - C15: live provider entitlement is out of scope.

## 1. What this report is

- **No new executions.** I only read files. I ran no commands, builds or tests, made no product calls or provider turns, and edited nothing.
- **Source of results.** Every native result cited here comes from QA session 01 (`Q/i4-448-independent-01`, 2026-11-21 09:00–09:17Z). Paths below are relative to that folder.
- **How QA01 ended.** It hit its usage quota, so it never produced a verdict:
  - `provider/result.json` records `is_error: true`, `api_error_status: 429`, `api_error: usage_limit_reached` and `terminal_reason: api_error`.
  - `provider/exit.json` records code 1.
  - The `subtype: "success"` field is a wrapper value, not a result.
  - `observations/criteria.json` is that session's per-criterion assessment, not a final verdict. This report gives the verdict; the original files are unchanged.
- **Not a review.** This is not a formal general review and doesn't reset the review budget. Both formal reviews are used up; the fresh GPT/Astra final audit is scan 3.

## 2. Code and build checks (C01)

- **Branches.** The QA branch `codex/gg-i4-448-qa` is still at `b45807f033601a53919f2c9e16e0de751971a518`, the worktree HEAD. The author branch `codex/gg-i4-448-preflight` is at `083d7264`; according to review-02's `b.patch`, it changes only the docs/11 table.
- **Clean tree.** Index and worktree were clean at 08:50:43Z and again at 09:16:34Z. The lockfile blob `92a751db…` is the same at base and head.
- **Runtime.** Node v22.23.4, pnpm 12.8.1.
- **Build.** One `pnpm build`: "12 successful, 12 total", **5 of them cache replays**, exit 0. It was not a fully uncached build.
- **Built output.** The built files call `projectStartupModelCatalog` at `settings.js:382`, `preflight.js:429` and `container.js:80`. The `apps/api/dist/main.js` SHA-256 `3160ac2a…` is the same in run-01, run-02 and the final state.
- **Diff.** 7 files, +393/−10. Nothing under `apps/web` changed.

## 3. Exact counts

These come from each run's `summary.json`. This corrects C14's "30 each".

| | run-01 | run-02 |
|---|---|---|
| Owned API child processes | **29** = 17 offline P cases + 12 startup (G0 plus S01–S11) | **30** = 18 P + 12 startup (G0 plus S01–S11) |
| Exit code 0 / exit code 1 | 13 / 16 | 14 / 16 (P18 is the extra exit 0) |
| Timed out | 0 | 0 |
| Still running (driver record) | none | none |
| Driver cases (pass / fail) | 40 (18 / 22) | 42 (41 / 1) |
| Checks (failed) | 515 (49) | 580 (1) |

- **Startup children.** There are 11 named startup scenarios plus the G0 first-run start: 12 startup child processes per run, not 11.
- **Exit records vs. process absence.** Exit codes and zero timeouts are the driver's own records. They don't prove that no process was left. That comes separately from two other records:
  - `binding/git-state-after.txt` at 09:16:34Z: `owned_process_refs=0`, `owner_port_listeners=0`.
  - `commands/30-cleanup.log`: both scratch roots removed after their nonces were checked (259 and 274 files), 27 test-suite TEMP leftovers removed, exit 0.
- **Stray wait loop.** The leftover bash wait loop (process tree from PID 40164, 4 PIDs) appears only in the QA01 provider event log (9 mentions), not in the cleanup log. I didn't trace it again.
- **Focused test tiers** are counted separately and not added together:
  - API: 61/61, exit 0.
  - Infrastructure: 55 passed / 1 failed, exit 1.

## 4. Per-criterion results

| ID | Result | Key evidence | Introduced by #448? |
|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | PASS | binding/*, commands/01-build.* | n/a |
| C02 | PASS | dist-binding.txt; run-02 M01 (9/9), P01, S01, S06 | Yes (the intended change) |

**Notes by criterion:**

- **C02.** Both the preflight and startup call sites use the same pure function. M01 shows stored rows keep their order, the input is not mutated, the call is idempotent and only missing (harness, model) pairs are added.
- **C03.** Preflight exits 0 with Database, Default model and Claude default model all ok. After P01 and P03 the stores still have 11 rows, with Terra and Opus absent.
- **C05.** The gateway starts and listens; healthz reports the owned child's PID. Both seeds show as enabled. `/system/model-defaults` equals GG_DEFAULTS. `/system/preflight` reports ok for the database and both default-model checks. The drained exit is 0. Stored rows go from 11 to 13; the migration ledger and format marker are unchanged, and no existing `enabled` flag changed. S02 covers rows missing only in the WAL, with the store inside GG_DATA_DIR.
- **C06.** A disabled stored row with the same seed ID stays a single, disabled row, both offline and after startup. A stored Claude effort list of `[high]` wins: `low` fails offline (P10) and is refused at startup with EFFORT_UNSUPPORTED (S09), while `high` passes (P11).
- **C07.**
  - Codex disabled default (P04): `WARN … is in the model catalog but disabled`, exit 0.
  - Claude disabled default (P05): `FAIL The configured Claude model is disabled`, exit 1.
  - At startup (S03/S04): the gateway boots and the row stays `enabled:false`. Validation reports MODEL_DISABLED as a warning and `publishable` is false. Publish is refused with 422 LOOP_INVALID. A run is accepted (202), then fails with EVALUATION_UNAVAILABLE / MODEL_DISABLED, and the fake CLIs see no model turn.
  - M03: `isAllowed` is false, `resolveHarnessModel` returns unavailable / MODEL_DISABLED, and `validateHarnessDefaults` returns `[]`.
  - D175 is about #442 plugin diagnostics and doesn't affect any of this.
